findings.title: Deleting cached data does not refresh the cache status where no onChanged is passed
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation only calls `onSuccess` (line 45). It does not invalidate `connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation in the same file does, in `onSettled` (lines 61-64). CalendarListContainer passes `onChanged`, which invalidates `connectedCalendars` (apps/web/components/apps/CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88, 112-113), so the main settings page refreshes. EventAdvancedTab renders the wrapper without `onChanged` (packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384), so `onSuccess` is undefined there. After a successful delete the toast says it worked, but the menu still shows 'Last updated' and 'Delete cached data' until the page reloads. Fix: move `const utils = trpc.useUtils();` above the cache mutation and add `async onSettled() { await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }` to `deleteCacheMutation`.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved against the caller's working directory and can write outside the repo
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current directory, and the script never changes directory. Run from the repo root as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, it writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into the parent directory of the repo and creates that file if it is missing (lines 62-70). The repo's env template is the root `.env.example`, so the intended target is the root `.env`. Fix: resolve it from the script location, e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`. Confidence is medium because the script documents no working directory, so the outcome depends on how it is run.

findings.title: Cache status bypasses the global calendar-cache gate that every other caller uses
findings.body: The handler constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly. Other callers go through `CalendarCache.init` (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28; e.g. packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:463, 616, 981), which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when calendar-cache is off globally. So the mock's new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-30) can never run from this path. With the flag off, the settings page still queries the table and shows 'Last updated' for any rows left behind. Fix: `const cacheRepository = await CalendarCache.init(null);`. That type-checks because the method is on the interface (calendar-cache.repository.interface.ts:30-32).

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted as en-US while the label is translated
findings.body: The label is localized through `t("cache_last_updated", …)`, but the timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` (lines 89-92). Users in other locales see an English date format inside a localized sentence. Format with the active locale instead.

findings.title: Legacy cache rows get the deploy time as 'Last updated'; header comment contradicts the statement
findings.body: `DEFAULT NOW()` gives every existing CalendarCache row the migration timestamp, so 'Last updated' shows the deploy date for rows not rewritten since. The real write time is recoverable: upsertCachedAvailability sets `expiresAt = now + CACHING_TIME` (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:16, 161, 168), so `expiresAt - 30 days` equals the write time if CACHING_TIME has always been 30 days. I could not confirm that from history. Separately, the generated header (lines 2-6) still says the column is added 'without a default value', which the next statement contradicts. Consider `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days';` after the ALTER, and correct the header.

findings.title: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped on every cache refresh but nothing in this part reads it
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every cache refresh (the webhook at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/webhook.ts:46 and unwatch at CalendarService.ts:975) and writes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every calendar under the credential. The status the UI shows reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29). `UserWithCalendars` carries the new field (packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28), but CalendarManager only uses `externalId` from selected calendars (packages/lib/CalendarManager.ts:81). Questions for the author: which consumer needs this column? And does Prisma write `@updatedAt` for an `updateMany` with empty `data`? If it does not, the line does no write at all and the PR's stated purpose is not met. If nothing reads it, the line is an extra UPDATE per webhook. My search for readers was not exhaustive.

findings.title: Cache delete bypasses the repository, though the PR says it uses the repository pattern
findings.body: The PR body says the cache deletion 'use[s] repository pattern', but this handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly, while the read path goes through the repository. The repository has no delete method, and the mock declares `deleteManyByCredential` (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:23-25) that the real class lacks. Moving the delete behind `CalendarCache.init` would be wrong as a drop-in: with the flag off it returns the mock, and the delete would silently do nothing while the toast says success. If the author moves it into the repository, the write must stay unconditional.

findings.title: No tests for the new delete handler, its ownership check, or the status query
findings.body: Nothing covers `deleteCacheHandler` and its ownership check (lines 17-26), `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188), or the enriched `connectedCalendarsHandler` output. The calendars folder has only setDestinationCalendar.handler.test.ts. The existing calendar-cache.repository.test.ts (prismock) already covers the repository, so a case for the new method fits there. The ownership check is the access boundary for this mutation, so it should have a test that a foreign credentialId is rejected.

findings.title: @calcom/platform-constants is imported but not declared by packages/features
findings.body: This file imports `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` from `@calcom/platform-constants`. packages/features/package.json does not declare that package, and this is the only import of it under packages/features. It resolves through workspace hoisting, but the package should list its own dependencies. Add it to packages/features/package.json, or import the constant from a package that already declares it.

findings.title: dev:cron runs npx tsx, but tsx is not declared anywhere in the repo
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. `tsx` does not appear in any package.json in the repo (ts-node is declared at apps/web/package.json:196). When tsx is not already installed, npx downloads the latest version on each run, unpinned. Add tsx to devDependencies, or keep ts-node, which is already declared. Confidence is medium because I did not check whether tsx is present transitively in node_modules.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD-only, and failure paths exit 0
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is the macOS form. On GNU sed (Linux) the empty string is read as the script and the command fails after tunnelmole has already started. Separately, `cleanup` always exits 0 (lines 11-18), and it is called on the rate-limit path (line 49) and the no-URL path (line 58), so a calling shell cannot tell the URL was not written. Consider `sed -i.bak` (works on both) with the .bak removed, and a non-zero exit on the failure paths.

findings.title: Reuse branch can write a stale tunnel URL from an old log
findings.body: In the 'already running' branch the URL comes from /tmp/tmole.log (line 30). That file is only cleared when this script starts tmole itself (line 34). If tmole was started elsewhere, the first URL in an older log can be written to the env file and reported as current, with no check that the log belongs to the running process.

contracts.action: Delete cached data: dropdown item, confirm dialog, then the deleteCache mutation
contracts.before_after: Disconnect invalidates connectedCalendars and integrations in onSettled. Cache delete invalidates nothing and only calls onSuccess, which is whatever the caller passed.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast. The status line and the menu item refresh only where onSuccess invalidates (CalendarListContainer.tsx:79-88, 112-113).
contracts.failure_mode: EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 passes no onChanged, so after a successful delete the menu still shows the old status until reload. The mutation outlives an unmount, and onSuccess still runs; no stale ref is kept.

contracts.action: deleteCache mutation: handler checks credential ownership, then deletes all CalendarCache rows for that credential
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:955 (unwatch deletes the same rows with the same credentialId filter, without an ownership check because it is internal)
contracts.before_after: Before the delete: findFirst on id and userId (deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22). The delete then uses credentialId only (deleteCache.handler.ts:28-30). Same delete as unwatch, plus the ownership check.
contracts.visible_effect: Success toast (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:44). The cached rows are gone and the next availability read recomputes.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing or foreign credential throws 'Credential not found or access denied' (deleteCache.handler.ts:24-26) and the component shows 'Error deleting cache' (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:47-49). A deleteMany error gives the same toast and touches nothing else. Cache-only data, so no retry journal is needed.

contracts.action: connectedCalendars query adds cacheUpdatedAt per credential
contracts.before_after: Sibling callers get CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is off globally, so no DB work. The new call always queries the table.
contracts.visible_effect: 'Last updated' appears for any credential that has cache rows, even when the flag is off.
contracts.failure_mode: If the groupBy rejects (for example the migration is not applied and updatedAt is missing), the whole connectedCalendars query rejects. There is no try/catch (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29), so the settings list fails to load instead of showing no status.

contracts.action: Error-state calendar card: Remove app now comes from the dropdown
contracts.before_after: Before: shown when !delegationCredentialId only. After: also hidden when disableConnectionModification is set (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68).
contracts.visible_effect: In the event-type Advanced tab (disableConnectionModification={true}, EventAdvancedTab.tsx:375) an error-state calendar loses its Remove button. This matches the card branch, but it is a behavior change the PR does not mention.

contracts.action: Remove app via dropdown: credentials.delete on the credential
contracts.before_after: The sibling disables its button when isDelegationCredential({credentialId}) (DisconnectIntegration.tsx:43, 49). The new dropdown checks only the delegationCredentialId prop (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:68).
contracts.visible_effect: If an in-memory delegation credential ever reaches the wrapper without delegationCredentialId, 'Remove app' is shown for it.
contracts.failure_mode: credentials.delete on that id would fail and show 'Error removing app' (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:58-60).
contracts.open_question: Do in-memory delegation credentials always reach the wrapper with delegationCredentialId set? CalendarManager sets it from credential.delegatedToId (CalendarManager.ts:65, 131), but I did not read where the in-memory credential's delegatedToId is set.

contracts.action: Cache refresh (webhook and unwatch) bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt via updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})
contracts.equivalent_path: none: no existing path bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
contracts.before_after: Before: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache wrote only CalendarCache rows. After: also an updateMany over every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including eventType-scoped ones.
contracts.visible_effect: None found in the files of this part; I found no reader of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.
contracts.failure_mode: If updateMany rejects after the cache write, fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache rejects. The webhook then returns an error (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/webhook.ts:46, defaultResponder), so Google retries. The cache write is already done and the retry is idempotent.
contracts.open_question: Which code reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt? Does Prisma set @updatedAt on updateMany with empty data?

contracts.action: findUnlockedUserForSession now selects updatedAt and googleChannelId on selectedCalendars
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:974-982 (findManyByIdsIncludeDestinationAndSelectedCalendars, uses include and so already returns full rows)
contracts.before_after: The narrow select now also returns updatedAt and googleChannelId. The other path already returned every column.
contracts.visible_effect: Server-side only (ctx.user, sessionMiddleware.ts:29). Client exposure not checked.
contracts.open_question: Does any tRPC procedure return ctx.user, or selectedCalendars taken from it, to the browser? If so, googleChannelId now goes out too.

contracts.action: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars
contracts.before_after: Every source selects full rows (include) or uses the updated select, so the widened type holds for each caller.

contracts.action: Migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW()
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/prisma/migrations/20250407204810_add_membership_creation_date/migration.sql (plain ADD COLUMN on an existing table)
contracts.before_after: Before: no updatedAt. After: every existing row gets the migration timestamp; the schema gets @default(now()) @updatedAt (schema.prisma:1719).
contracts.visible_effect: 'Last updated' for rows not rewritten since the deploy shows the deploy date.

contracts.action: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh: rm -f the log, start tmole, then write GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into ENV_FILE
contracts.equivalent_path: none. The repo's env template is the root .env.example.
contracts.before_after: The script deletes /tmp/tmole.log only when it starts tmole itself, then rewrites or appends the env line.
contracts.visible_effect: Writes the tunnel URL into the env file and prints success.
contracts.failure_mode: Run from the repo root, it writes to the parent directory (finding). sed -i '' is BSD-only. The reuse branch can use a stale log URL. cleanup exits 0 on failure. The rm targets a fixed /tmp path and removes a symlink rather than its target, so the risk is low.

contracts.action: dev:cron now runs npx tsx instead of ts-node
contracts.before_after: Before: ts-node, declared. After: npx tsx, not declared anywhere in the repo.
contracts.failure_mode: When tsx is not installed, npx fetches the latest version from the registry on each run.

summary: No blockers in this part. Two findings should be fixed in this pull request: (1) the new "Delete cached data" action never refreshes the cache status in the event-type Advanced tab, because the dropdown does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` itself as the disconnect path does; (2) `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` resolves `ENV_FILE` against the caller's working directory, so run from the repo root it writes to the parent directory. The rest are consider-level: the cache-status query bypasses the `CalendarCache.init` gate every other caller uses, the `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` bump has no reader I could find, legacy rows show the deploy date, the cache-status date is hard-coded to en-US, the new handler and status query have no tests, `@calcom/platform-constants` and `tsx` are undeclared, and the script has macOS-only `sed` and a stale-log reuse risk. The widened `UserWithCalendars` type holds for every caller I checked. Method: static reading only; nothing was built, run or tested. `user.ts`, `schema.prisma` and `common.json` were read in the changed regions and their surroundings, not in full; I report nothing on them.

notices: Contract "Migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW()": evidence not verified: packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:16,161,168 is not path:line.
